name: GitHub
label: git push --set-upstream origin prod
summary: Self-serve and nobody reviews it. The only humans in your way are the organization owners of your customers.
verdict: An hour of setup, and nobody reviews it. The only people who can hold you up are your customers' own org owners.
blocker: Customers in organizations with OAuth app restrictions will see only public data until an org owner approves you.

steps.title: Open Developer settings
steps.detail: Under your account, or an organization you administer: Settings, Developer settings, OAuth apps, New OAuth App. Create it under an organization if the company, not you, should own it.

steps.title: Fill in the registration form
steps.detail: Four fields and one checkbox. The callback URL is the one that matters, and you only get one.

fields.label: Application name
fields.value: Public. Don't put internal URLs here.

fields.label: Homepage URL
fields.value: Full URL of your app's site

fields.label: Device Flow
fields.value: Tick only if you use the device flow

steps.title: Copy the client ID, generate a client secret
steps.detail: The page we read doesn't describe credentials, so this is from how the console behaves in practice. Put both in your secret store, never in the repo.

steps.title: Wire the callback and request the narrowest scopes
steps.detail: Add the callback route and read the credentials from env. Scopes are coarse: you can't scope source access to read-only, so ask only for what the feature needs.

steps.title: Authorize against your own account
steps.detail: Your email must be verified before GitHub lets you authorize any OAuth app. Run the flow once end to end before you share anything.

steps.title: Customers in restricted orgs: an owner has to approve you
steps.detail: Restrictions are on by default for new organizations. Until an owner approves, your app gets public resources only. How long that takes depends on the owner, not on GitHub.

nuances.text: An OAuth app has a single callback URL. GitHub Apps can have several.
nuances.note: Practical effect: register a second OAuth app for localhost.

nuances.text: OAuth apps act only on behalf of a user, never as an installation.
A token can't exceed its owner's access. An admin:org token still has no org admin rights if the user isn't an owner.
Up to 10 tokens per user, app and scope set. The 11th revokes an old one. Over 10 creations in an hour triggers a re-authorization prompt instead.
SAML SSO orgs need an active SAML session each time a user authorizes.
Neither page we read mentions a review or approval step for the provider side.
nuances.note: That is absence of a mention, not a statement that none exists.

nuances.text: For new integrations a GitHub App is usually the better fit: finer permissions, expiring tokens, per-repo installs.
nuances.note: Our read, not from the pages above. Worth checking before you commit.

blockers.cause: The callback in your request doesn't match the one registered. With one callback per app, local and prod collide.
blockers.fix: Register a separate OAuth app per environment.

blockers.symptom: App can't see an org's private repos
blockers.cause: The org restricts OAuth apps and nobody approved yours.
blockers.fix: Ask an owner to approve it. Users can send an approval request from the authorization page.

blockers.symptom: Users keep getting the authorize screen again
blockers.cause: More than 10 token creations per hour for the same user, app and scopes.
blockers.fix: Store and reuse tokens instead of re-running the flow.

blockers.symptom: 403 on an org with SAML SSO
blockers.cause: No active SAML session when the user authorized.
blockers.fix: Revoke the app, sign in to the org to start a SAML session, authorize again.

agent: Add the callback route and env wiring to your repo
Pick the narrowest scopes for the feature
Draft the approval request your customers' org owners will need
Run a test authorization once credentials are in .env
you: Sign in and register the app (it's bound to your account)
Get each customer org owner to approve the app

redirect.rule: One callback URL per OAuth app. Use one app per environment.

scopes.name: repo
scopes.note: Full private repo access. Restricted orgs withhold it until approved.
